messages:
Arun: kicked off customer 'orchid' LoRA merge onto base-xl int4 this morning. quick smoke with our 'formatting-telemetry' pack shows odd tokenization/spacing for currency and percentages. opening thread to triage.
Leah: can you drop the eval link and a minimal repro command?
Arun: eval id internal: https://redwood.internal/evals/ORCH-47 (private)
Arun: repro command:
```bash
./bin/quick_eval --model=orchid-lora-merged-int4 --eval=formatting-telemetry --limit=250 --seed=99 --out=orchid_out.json
```
Ben: paste a short failing example (baseline vs merged) so we can see detok artifacts
Arun: example:
```text
PROMPT: "Subtotal: $" + subtotal + "\nTax (8.5%): "
BASELINE (fp32): "Subtotal: $123.45
Tax (8.5%): $10.49
MERGED-INT4: "Subtotal: $123 .45
Tax (8.5%): $10 .4 9
```
Leah: interesting — spaces inside numeric tokens and split digits. Could be tokenizer id remapping or int4-induced token fragmentation. do we have the tokenizer bundle used to train the LoRA?
Arun: customer supplied a custom BPE with numeric normalization step; our merge used standard bpe-v2. I uploaded their tokenizer to /cust/orchid/tokenizer.json.
Ben: two quick experiments: 1) rerun eval forcing their tokenizer: `--tokenizer=/cust/orchid/tokenizer.json` to see if detok fixes, 2) run merged-int8 to isolate quant effects.
infra-bot: job scheduled on gpu-test-2 (1xA100) for 30m window. job ids: 10911 (cust-tokenizer), 10912 (merged-int8).
Arun: ran both. results n=250: EM_format fp32=0.995, merged-int8=0.992, merged-int4=0.74. rerun-with-cust-tokenizer for int4 improved to 0.92.
Leah: that suggests token mismatch is primary, quant amplifies it. note the large gap between int8 and int4. any telemetry on which layers show large outliers?
Ben: yes — profiling shows layernorm 7 and attention output proj have high outlier magnitudes in weight deltas after LoRA merge; int4 quantizer produced large rounding errors there. attaching short profiler snippet: `top_outliers: [{layer: "attn_out", pct: 0.12}, {layer: "ln_7", pct:0.09}]` (uploaded).
Arun: plan: 1) for short-term, remap LoRA deltas to customer's tokenizer and remerge (fast), 2) apply per-layer outlier-clipping before int4 quant for those layers and re-evaluate, 3) if needed, publish an int8 fallback route for billing endpoints.
Leah: add a decode shim option too: map token ids at detokenize time when route is tagged for this customer. cheap patch, but brittle. prefer remap+remerge.
CS-Eng: customer is sensitive — invoices being slightly misformatted is a blocker. please prioritize remap and a canary. also draft a short CS note explaining rollback steps.
Arun: started remap job `remap-lora --lora=orchid_lora.pt --src-map=trained_tokenmap.json --dst-map=/cust/orchid/tokenizer.json` and then `merge-weights --base=base-xl --lora=remapped_lora.pt --out=orchid-merged-remap.pt`. infra-bot: remap job 10920 queued.
Ben: when re-quantizing for int4, try using `--quant-rule=per-channel-clamp --clip-threshold=3.5` and `--preserve-kv-scale` flags; these helped on a previous customer. Also test `--no-prefix-cache` as prefix cache can mask token alignment issues in some runtimes.
Arun: will run ablation matrix: [fp32, int8, int4(default), int4+clip] x [standard-tokenizer, cust-tokenizer]. posting results when done.
infra-bot: job 10920 started on gpu-test-2. ETA 12m.
Leah: follow-up: we should add a token-alignment check to the LoRA onboarding checklist (numeric/punctuation token overlap >99.9%) and a recommended remap step if mismatch. filing a tiny RFC.
Arun: agreed. also adding a telemetry alarm: if EM_format drops >5% post-merge on billing pack, block default rollout.
CS-Eng: thanks. we'll hold rollout until remap results are verified and will enable int8 fallback for production route meanwhile.
Arun: thanks team — will report back with artifacts and a short KB blurb for CS. :white_check_mark:
